## What is Claude Design (claude.ai/design)? 11


min read


Reading Time:


8


minutes


Claude Design is Anthropic’s chat-to-canvas design product. You describe what you want in plain language, Claude builds a first version on a canvas, and you refine it through chat, inline comments, and direct edits. The product lives at[claude.ai/design](https://claude.ai/design) (also linked from Claude’s product page) and in the Claude desktop sidebar.


It is not Figma, not a generic image generator, and not a full production frontend builder by itself. It is a conversational design workspace for prototypes, decks, one-pagers, marketing visuals, and interactive concepts, with optional design-system context and a handoff path into Claude Code.


If you searched “what is Claude Design” because the SERP is noisy, this page is the short answer first, then the practical workflow, then where Anima and AgentGrid.io fit when you need Figma continuity or a durable shared artifact.


For ChatGPT users,[Claude Design alternative would be ChatGPT+AgentGrid.io](https://chatgpt.com/plugins/plugin_asdk_app_6a747c2caadc8191acf784bd04153268) , offering the sharing, versioning, collaboration and publishing features directly from the chat.


## Short answer


Question Answer


What is it? Anthropic Labs product for creating visual work with Claude on a dedicated canvas


Where?[claude.ai/design](https://claude.ai/design) and Claude Desktop sidebar


Who can use it? Claude Pro, Max, Team, and Enterprise (Enterprise often off by default until an admin enables it)


Model / status Launched in research preview on April 17, 2026; later described as beta. Powered at launch by Claude Opus 4.7 (model may change)


Best for Fast exploration, PM mockups, decks, marketing concepts, Claude-native handoff to Claude Code


Not a replacement for Deep Figma design-system work, pixel-level craft, or multi-agent artifact collaboration outside Claude


Anthropic’s launch post frames the problem clearly: designers ration exploration because there is rarely time for a dozen directions, and non-designers struggle to turn an idea into something shareable. Claude Design is their answer to both.


## How Claude Design works


Claude Design splits the screen: chat on the left, canvas on the right. Anthropic’s help center describes the loop as:


1. Create a project
2. Attach or import a design system when you have one
3. Add context (screenshots, docs, codebase)
4. Describe what you want
5. Review the canvas result
6. Refine with chat, inline comments, or direct canvas edits
7. Export or share


Anthropic’s own guidance is useful here: the first generation is a starting point. The value is iteration.


Claude Design features overview (Anima blog asset)


### What you can make


Typical outputs called out by Anthropic and help docs:


- Product wireframes and app screens
- Landing pages and marketing collateral
- Pitch decks and presentations
- Interactive prototypes
- One-pagers and social visuals
- Code-powered frontier prototypes (voice, video, shaders, 3D, built-in AI), when that path is supported


### Design systems and brand


Claude Design can import design systems from GitHub, design files, uploads, or a local codebase (including via` /design-sync` from Claude Code). Claude is supposed to build with your components and check output against the system before you see it. Team and Enterprise admins can lock a standard system.


That matters because generic AI UI is the default failure mode in this category. Brand context is the difference between a demo and something a PM can put in a review.


### Export and handoff


Documented export and send destinations include PDF, PPTX, standalone HTML, zip/folder, Canva, and connectors such as Adobe, Gamma, Lovable, Miro, Replit, Vercel, and Wix (lists change; recheck current docs before you promise a connector).


The Claude-native build path is handoff to Claude Code: package the design and continue from the working project instead of rebuilding from a screenshot.


**Important workflow gap for many design teams:** Claude Design does not offer a native Figma export. If Figma is your source of truth, you need an extra bridge.

## Where Claude Design fits (and where it stops)


### Strong fit


- You already live in Claude and Claude Code
- You need a visual in the same meeting, not next week
- A PM or founder needs a mockup or deck before design capacity opens up
- You want organization-scoped sharing inside Claude


### Weak fit (today)


- Your designers need native Figma components, variants, and file hygiene
- You need multi-model collaboration on the same durable artifact (Claude + ChatGPT + a coding agent + a human editor)
- You need a public website with custom domain, version history across agents, or AgentGrid-style publish controls
- You need reliable multiplayer editing (Anthropic still calls simultaneous multi-person editing basic)


Be fair: Claude Design is excellent at conversation-to-canvas. It is not trying to be every design tool.


## Practical workflow after Claude Design


Here is the useful end-to-end path for teams that care about brand, Figma, and shippable product UI.


### 1. Explore in Claude Design


Start at[claude.ai/design](https://claude.ai/design) . Prompt for 2-3 directions. Attach screenshots or a design system. Iterate until the story is clear.


### 2. Continue in Figma when craft matters


If the next owner is a designer, move the concept into Figma. Anima’s Buddy can turn Claude Design HTML into editable Figma layers so you are not stuck outside the design system. Guide:[How to go from Claude Design to Figma](https://www.animaapp.com/blog/genai/how-to-go-from-claude-design-to-figma/) .


Claude Design to Figma with Anima Buddy


### 3. Build a working prototype in Anima Playground


When you need an on-brand, editable HTML/React prototype (not only a canvas mockup), continue in[Anima Playground](https://www.animaapp.com/) . Start from prompt, Figma, image, or URL. Keep Playground, Buddy, and Figma-to-code distinct. Playground is the browser app/prototype surface. Buddy is the Figma AI agent.


Anima Playground


### 4. Fill gaps Claude Design does not own alone


Example: Claude Design is weak at generating marketing images for the pages it builds. Teams can put the design on AgentGrid.io and let ChatGPT generate images into the same artifact. Guide:[Generate images for Claude Design with ChatGPT](https://www.animaapp.com/blog/genai/generate-images-for-claude-design-with-chatgpt/) .


Generate images for Claude Design with ChatGPT via AgentGrid.io


### 5. Publish or share a durable artifact on AgentGrid.io


If the result must leave one chat, survive version history, and stay editable by people and other agents, move it to[AgentGrid.io](https://agentgrid.io/) . That is the shared workspace for live artifacts (docs, apps, designs), not a second design canvas. Guide:[Publish a Claude Design website with AgentGrid.io](https://www.animaapp.com/blog/agentic/publish-claude-design-website-agentgrid/) .

## FAQ


### Is Claude Design the same as Claude Artifacts?


No. Artifacts are outputs beside a Claude chat (often documents, HTML, or code). Claude Design is a dedicated design product with its own canvas, project model, and export/handoff flows at claude.ai/design.


### Is Claude Design free?


It is included with Claude Pro, Max, Team, and Enterprise subscriptions and counts toward plan usage limits (Anthropic previously had a separate weekly Design allowance; current help docs say Design now shares the plan pool). Enterprise is typically off until an admin enables it. Recheck[Anthropic pricing and help](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/14604416-get-started-with-claude-design) before publishing plan claims.


### Can Claude Design replace Figma?


Not as a full replacement for most product design orgs. It is strong for speed and exploration. Figma remains stronger for component systems, variants, and design-file operations. Use Buddy when you need the AI step inside Figma.


### How do I open Claude Design?


Go to[claude.ai/design](https://claude.ai/design) , or open it from the Claude desktop sidebar. Official product marketing also points to[claude.com/product/design](https://claude.com/product/design) .


## Bottom line


Claude Design is Anthropic’s answer to “describe it, see it, refine it” for visual work. Use it when Claude is already your workspace and speed matters. When the next step is Figma craft, a real product prototype, image generation across agents, or a durable shared artifact, continue with Buddy, Anima Playground, or AgentGrid.io instead of forcing Claude Design to be the whole stack.
